sections.html:
Because Athens and Clarke County merged into a single government, one office, the Athens-Clarke County Property Tax Division, sends the bill for the whole county. Payments fund the Clarke County Board of Education, Athens-Clarke County and the State of Georgia.

October 20 is the general due date for real estate and business personal property. A bill left unpaid can be levied on and eventually sold. Beyond interest, the division adds a 5% penalty at each 120-day mark after the due date, up to four times, for a possible 20% total.

  • Land and buildings are taxed where they are located, under O.C.G.A. 48-5-11.
  • Taxable value is 40% of market value, with exceptions written into law (O.C.G.A. 48-5-7).
  • Standing timber is not taxed until it is sold or cut, then it is taxed at 100% of its fair market value.

Each bill shows both the fair market value and the assessed value, so you can see what the assessors used before you decide whether to appeal.

Clarke is Georgia's smallest county by area, at 121 square miles including 1.8 of water. Athens and Winterville are the cities, and the town of Bogart lies mostly in Oconee County. The University of Georgia shapes the housing market.

The 2025 estimate is 129,921 people, just 1.0% above the 2020 base. Owners live in only 41.4% of homes, so most households rent, and typical rent is $1,219. An owner-held home has a median value of $298,900 and median household income is $53,625. Many Athens houses are rentals, and an investor-owned home gets the same bill as any other.

Send a written appeal to the Board of Assessors within 45 days of the day the assessment notice was mailed. When the assessors keep the value, your file goes to the Board of Equalization automatically. The Athens-Clarke assessors answer questions at 706-613-3140.

Athens-Clarke appeal timeline
StepTiming
Written appeal delivered to the assessors45 days from notice mailing
Board of Equalization notifies both sides of hearing date15 days after the appeal reaches that board
Hearing held20 to 30 days after that letter
Appeal to Superior CourtWritten, 30 days after the Board of Equalization rules

At the hearing the assessors' appraiser presents comparable sales first, then you present your evidence, the Board of Equalization asks questions, and a ruling goes to both sides. Arbitration and a hearing officer are the other two methods the state allows, and the assessors' office can explain them.

sections.h2: Returns you may need to file
sections.html:
File the real estate return, Form PT-50R, with the tax commissioner in room 250 of the Courthouse before filing season closes April 1, in any year you acquired or altered the property. Nothing has changed since last year? Then you may skip it. A required return that is not filed draws a 10% penalty on the value not returned, plus interest and possibly other penalties.

Personal property has a tougher rule: Form PT-50P goes to the Board of Assessors every April 1, changed or not. The tax commissioner also warns buyers of businesses, boats and aircraft to check for unpaid personal property tax before closing, since attorneys usually search real estate taxes only.

The state homestead exemption belongs to people who own a home and live in it as their primary residence. You can apply whenever you like, but to start in a given year the application must be in by April 1, and not applying counts as waiving it. Some counties add larger local exemptions, so ask the Athens-Clarke offices which ones apply to a given house before you assume the standard amount is all there is.

If tax was assessed and collected in error or illegally, you may request a refund in writing, provided you begin the request within three years of payment. When an assessment is under appeal and the final taxable value comes in lower, the refund is processed automatically once that value is final. Equipment, machinery and fixtures used by a business are assessed at 40% of fair market value, and the assessor may value a going business as a whole.

sections.h2: What happens if taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Athens-Clarke County runs its own tax sales. The tax commissioner serves as ex officio sheriff, and Georgia law requires the property to be advertised for four consecutive weeks in the legal section of the county newspaper, the Athens Banner-Herald.

  • Sales begin at 10:00 a.m. on the first Tuesday of the month, ordinarily in front of the courthouse, and run as a public outcry auction.
  • The opening bid equals the taxes due plus costs, and the property goes to the highest bidder or may be bid in for the county.
  • Payment is due at the sale, by cashier's or certified check from an FDIC-insured institution.
  • The tax commissioner then executes and records a tax deed. The purchaser owes taxes as they come due, and any amount paid may be added to the redemption price.

An owner who sees a notice for their address should contact the tax commissioner at once. Redemption rights exist under Georgia law, and the county's tax sale page has the current list of properties.

sections.h2: What should I settle at closing when selling in Clarke County?
sections.html:
The owner in January pays the year's tax, and nothing is refunded for the months after a sale. Whether the buyer credits you for their share of the year is a matter the two of you settle on the closing statement.

Interest does not start until 60 days after the bill's postmark. If October 20 has gone by and a balance remains, ask for a payoff figure that includes penalties and pay it from the sale proceeds so the title is clear.

Rental owners selling an occupied house should confirm that business personal property, such as appliances listed on a business return, has no balance. Questions about exemptions, returns or values go to the assessors, and bills and payments go to the Property Tax Division.

sections.h2: Steps for a Clarke County seller
sections.html:
Read your latest bill first, since it lists both market and assessed value. Call the Property Tax Division for the balance. If the value looks wrong and your 45 days are not over, call the assessors at 706-613-3140. Landlords should ask whether a business return lists items that carry their own tax.

A cash sale uses the same payoff process as a financed one, so request the figure early and give it to the closing attorney. The buyer files their own homestead application by April 1 once they move in.

faqs.q: What is the Athens-Clarke County due date?
faqs.a: October 20 in the usual case. The Property Tax Division lists that date for real estate and business personal property.

faqs.q: What is the Athens-Clarke County appeal window?
faqs.a: It is 45 days from the day the assessment notice was mailed. Send the appeal in writing to the Board of Assessors, and call 706-613-3140 with questions.

faqs.q: Who conducts tax sales in Clarke County?
faqs.a: The tax commissioner, acting as ex officio sheriff. Auctions start at 10:00 a.m. on each month's first Tuesday, usually in front of the courthouse.

faqs.q: Must I file a property return every year in Athens-Clarke County?
faqs.a: Not for real estate if nothing changed. Real estate returns are due January 1 to April 1 in years the property changed or was acquired, while personal property returns are due every April 1.

faqs.q: Do most Clarke County residents own their homes?
faqs.a: No. Owners live in 41.4% of homes for 2020 to 2024, so renters are the majority.
